blocks.en: 🌍 World Missions — Unit 4: Acts 1:8 and the Spreading Gospel
blocks.es_reference: 🌍 Misiones Mundiales — Unidad 4: Hechos 1:8 y el Evangelio que Se Esparce

blocks.en: Professor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers
blocks.es_reference: Profesor: Dr. Wayne Cook | Director: Dr. Ted Rogers

blocks.en: Introduction: The Book That Has No Ending
blocks.es_reference: Introducción: El Libro Que No Tiene Final

blocks.en: Open the book of Acts and read its very first sentence: "The former account I made, O Theophilus, of all that Jesus began both to do and teach" (Acts 1:1, NKJV). Notice the word "began." Luke does not say his Gospel told all that Jesus did; it told all that Jesus began to do. Acts is volume two — the record of what the risen, ascended Lord continued to do and teach through His Spirit-filled church. And the book has no formal ending, because the work is not finished. We are living in the long second volume.
blocks.es_reference: Abra el libro de los Hechos y lea su primera frase: "En el primer tratado, oh Teófilo, he hablado de todas las cosas que Jesús comenzó a hacer y a enseñar" (Hechos 1:1, RVG). Note la palabra "comenzó." Lucas no dice que su Evangelio contó todo lo que Jesús hizo; contó todo lo que Jesús comenzó a hacer. Hechos es el volumen dos — el registro de lo que el Señor resucitado y ascendido continuó haciendo y enseñando por medio de su iglesia llena del Espíritu. Y el libro no tiene final formal, porque la obra no ha terminado. Vivimos en el largo segundo volumen.

blocks.en: If the four Gospels are the vertical dimension of our faith — the Father sending the Son, the Son obeying to the cross — then Acts is the horizontal dimension. It shows the gospel running outward from a small group in Jerusalem to a worldwide community of every nation under heaven. Acts is, in a real sense, the first missions textbook. And the whole of it grows out of a single verse.
blocks.es_reference: Si los cuatro Evangelios son la dimensión vertical de nuestra fe — el Padre enviando al Hijo, el Hijo obedeciendo hasta la cruz — entonces Hechos es la dimensión horizontal. Muestra el evangelio corriendo hacia afuera desde un pequeño grupo en Jerusalén hasta una comunidad mundial de toda nación debajo del cielo. Hechos es, en un sentido real, el primer libro de texto de misiones. Y todo él brota de un solo versículo.

blocks.en: I. The Last Command and the Table of Contents
blocks.es_reference: I. El Último Mandato y la Tabla de Contenido

blocks.en: Before He ascended, Jesus gave His disciples one last promise and one last assignment: "You shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth" (Acts 1:8, NKJV). That single verse is the table of contents of the entire book. Chapters 1 through 7 tell of the witness in Jerusalem. Chapters 8 through 12 carry it into Judea and Samaria. Chapters 13 through 28 take it to the end of the earth.
blocks.es_reference: Antes de ascender, Jesús dio a sus discípulos una última promesa y una última encomienda: "Recibiréis poder cuando haya venido sobre vosotros el Espíritu Santo, y me seréis testigos en Jerusalén, en toda Judea, en Samaria, y hasta lo último de la tierra" (Hechos 1:8, RVG). Ese solo versículo es la tabla de contenido del libro entero. Los capítulos 1 al 7 hablan del testimonio en Jerusalén. Los capítulos 8 al 12 lo llevan a Judea y Samaria. Los capítulos 13 al 28 lo llevan hasta lo último de la tierra.

blocks.en: Look closely at the pattern, for it is the pattern of all missions. The gospel begins at home, in Jerusalem. It moves next to the near neighbor — Judea, the surrounding region, and Samaria, the people most despised. And it presses on to the end of the earth, to the peoples who have never heard. Home, near, and far: the rings widen, but not one ring is to be skipped, and not one is to be the stopping place. The same command that sent the apostles is the command that reaches us, for we live at the far edge of those widening circles.
blocks.es_reference: Mire de cerca el patrón, porque es el patrón de todas las misiones. El evangelio comienza en casa, en Jerusalén. Pasa luego al vecino cercano — Judea, la región circundante, y Samaria, el pueblo más despreciado. Y avanza hasta lo último de la tierra, a los pueblos que nunca han oído. Casa, cerca y lejos: los anillos se ensanchan, pero ningún anillo ha de saltarse, y ninguno ha de ser el punto de detención. El mismo mandato que envió a los apóstoles es el mandato que nos alcanza a nosotros, porque vivimos en el borde más lejano de esos círculos que se ensanchan.

blocks.en: II. Power Before Program
blocks.es_reference: II. El Poder Antes del Programa

blocks.en: Notice what came first. Before the program of Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria, and the end of the earth, there was a power: "You shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you." Jesus had told them plainly, "do not depart from Jerusalem, but wait for the Promise of the Father" (Acts 1:4, NKJV). They were not to launch the mission in their own strength. They were to wait for the Holy Spirit. And at Pentecost the Spirit came, the church was born, and the same hundred and twenty who had been hiding behind locked doors went out and turned the city upside down.
blocks.es_reference: Note lo que vino primero. Antes del programa de Jerusalén, Judea, Samaria y lo último de la tierra, hubo un poder: "Recibiréis poder cuando haya venido sobre vosotros el Espíritu Santo." Jesús les había dicho claramente: "no os fueseis de Jerusalén, sino que esperaseis la promesa del Padre" (Hechos 1:4, RVG). No habían de lanzar la misión en sus propias fuerzas. Habían de esperar al Espíritu Santo. Y en Pentecostés el Espíritu vino, la iglesia nació, y los mismos ciento veinte que se habían escondido tras puertas cerradas salieron y trastornaron la ciudad.

blocks.en: Here is a truth we dare not forget: missions is the work of the Holy Spirit through the church. The strategies, the funds, and the training all have their place, but without the power of the Spirit they accomplish nothing. The book of Acts could just as well be called the Acts of the Holy Spirit, for it is He who drives the gospel outward through every chapter.
blocks.es_reference: He aquí una verdad que no nos atrevemos a olvidar: las misiones son la obra del Espíritu Santo por medio de la iglesia. Las estrategias, los fondos y el entrenamiento tienen su lugar, pero sin el poder del Espíritu no logran nada. El libro de los Hechos bien podría llamarse los Hechos del Espíritu Santo, porque es Él quien impulsa el evangelio hacia afuera por cada capítulo.

blocks.en: III. The Church That Would Not Leave Home
blocks.es_reference: III. La Iglesia Que No Quería Salir de Casa

blocks.en: And yet, for all that power, there was a problem. Acts 1:8 had been spoken from the Master's own lips. Pentecost had come and gone. Three thousand were saved, and then five thousand. And every one of those new believers was still in Jerusalem. The command to carry the gospel to Judea, Samaria, and the end of the earth was a fine thing — as long as it did not require anyone to leave home.
blocks.es_reference: Y sin embargo, a pesar de todo aquel poder, había un problema. Hechos 1:8 había sido pronunciado por los labios mismos del Maestro. Pentecostés había venido y pasado. Tres mil fueron salvos, y luego cinco mil. Y cada uno de aquellos nuevos creyentes seguía en Jerusalén. El mandato de llevar el evangelio a Judea, Samaria y lo último de la tierra era cosa buena — mientras no requiriera que nadie saliera de casa.

blocks.en: We must be honest enough to see ourselves here. It is easy to love the Great Commission in the abstract and never cross the city limits of our own comfortable Jerusalem. The first believers had the command, the power, and the message, and still they stayed. God had to move them.
blocks.es_reference: Debemos ser lo bastante honestos para vernos aquí. Es fácil amar la Gran Comisión en lo abstracto y nunca cruzar los límites de nuestra propia y cómoda Jerusalén. Los primeros creyentes tenían el mandato, el poder y el mensaje, y aun así se quedaron. Dios tuvo que moverlos.

blocks.en: IV. Scattered Means Sown
blocks.es_reference: IV. Esparcidos Quiere Decir Sembrados

blocks.en: And move them He did, through the fire of persecution. When Stephen was martyred, a great persecution broke out, and the believers were driven out of Jerusalem. Luke chooses his words with care. The verb he uses in Acts 8:4 comes from the root that means to sow — to fling seed across a plowed field, the very word Jesus used in the parable of the sower. Saul of Tarsus thought he was destroying a movement. He was, in fact, planting a crop. "Therefore those who were scattered went everywhere preaching the word" (Acts 8:4, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: Y los movió, por medio del fuego de la persecución. Cuando Esteban fue martirizado, estalló una gran persecución, y los creyentes fueron expulsados de Jerusalén. Lucas escoge sus palabras con cuidado. El verbo que usa en Hechos 8:4 viene de la raíz que significa sembrar — esparcir la semilla por el campo arado, la misma palabra que Jesús usó en la parábola del sembrador. Saulo de Tarso creía que estaba destruyendo un movimiento. En realidad, estaba plantando una cosecha. "Pero los que fueron esparcidos, iban por todas partes predicando la palabra" (Hechos 8:4, RVG).

blocks.en: Persecution did not dissipate the gospel; it disseminated it. The believers who lost their homes and their livelihoods carried the message into Judea and Samaria as they ran. Philip preached in a Samaritan city, and later to an Ethiopian official on a desert road. The second ring of Acts 1:8 was being filled — not by a comfortable, well-planned campaign, but by ordinary scattered believers who could not stop speaking of Christ.
blocks.es_reference: La persecución no disipó el evangelio; lo diseminó. Los creyentes que perdieron sus casas y su sustento llevaron el mensaje a Judea y Samaria mientras huían. Felipe predicó en una ciudad de Samaria, y más tarde a un funcionario etíope en un camino desierto. El segundo anillo de Hechos 1:8 se estaba llenando — no por una campaña cómoda y bien planeada, sino por creyentes comunes y esparcidos que no podían dejar de hablar de Cristo.

blocks.en: V. The Barrier Falls
blocks.es_reference: V. El Muro Cae

blocks.en: There remained the hardest barrier of all — the wall between Jew and Gentile. God tore it down. He gave the apostle Peter a vision on a rooftop in Joppa and then sent him to the house of Cornelius, a Roman centurion. There Peter spoke words that opened the door of the gospel to the whole world: "In truth I perceive that God shows no partiality. But in every nation whoever fears Him and works righteousness is accepted by Him" (Acts 10:34–35, NKJV). The Holy Spirit fell on those Gentiles just as He had on the Jews at Pentecost, and the matter was settled.
blocks.es_reference: Quedaba la barrera más difícil de todas — el muro entre judío y gentil. Dios lo derribó. Dio al apóstol Pedro una visión en una azotea en Jope y luego lo envió a la casa de Cornelio, un centurión romano. Allí Pedro habló palabras que abrieron la puerta del evangelio al mundo entero: "En verdad entiendo que Dios no hace acepción de personas; sino que en toda nación, el que le teme y obra justicia, le es acepto" (Hechos 10:34–35, RVG). El Espíritu Santo cayó sobre aquellos gentiles tal como había caído sobre los judíos en Pentecostés, y el asunto quedó resuelto.

blocks.en: It was in the great Gentile city of Antioch that the gospel found its next center of gravity, and there "the disciples were first called Christians" (Acts 11:26, NKJV). The faith of Israel's Messiah had become the faith of the nations.
blocks.es_reference: Fue en la gran ciudad gentil de Antioquía donde el evangelio halló su siguiente centro de gravedad, y allí "los discípulos fueron llamados cristianos por primera vez" (Hechos 11:26, RVG). La fe del Mesías de Israel se había vuelto la fe de las naciones.

blocks.en: VI. Antioch, the First Sending Church
blocks.es_reference: VI. Antioquía, la Primera Iglesia Que Envía

blocks.en: Now the third ring opens. Open Acts 13. Antioch has become the cutting edge of the movement, and five men are leading the church there: Barnabas the Cypriot, Simeon called Niger, Lucius of Cyrene, Manaen who had been raised in Herod's own palace, and Saul the former persecutor. It was the first multi-ethnic leadership team in the history of the church, and they were together fasting and ministering to the Lord when the Spirit spoke: "Now separate to Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them" (Acts 13:2, NKJV).
blocks.es_reference: Ahora se abre el tercer anillo. Abra Hechos 13. Antioquía se ha vuelto el filo del movimiento, y cinco hombres dirigen la iglesia allí: Bernabé el chipriota, Simeón llamado Niger, Lucio de Cirene, Manaén que se había criado en el palacio mismo de Herodes, y Saulo el ex perseguidor. Era el primer equipo de liderazgo multiétnico en la historia de la iglesia, y estaban juntos ayunando y ministrando al Señor cuando el Espíritu habló: "Apartadme a Bernabé y a Saulo para la obra a la cual los he llamado" (Hechos 13:2, RVG).

blocks.en: Watch what the church did. "Having fasted and prayed, and laid hands on them, they sent them away" (Acts 13:3, NKJV). And watch how Luke describes it in the very next breath: "So, being sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia" (Acts 13:4, NKJV). Antioch sent them. The Holy Spirit sent them. Both are true. Here is the first sending church, and here is the pattern that has never changed: the Spirit calls workers out of a praying, fasting, worshiping congregation, and the church lays hands on them and sends them to the end of the earth. This is the same burden we saw the Lord place on our hearts in the Great Commission.
blocks.es_reference: Observe lo que hizo la iglesia. "Habiendo ayunado y orado, y puesto las manos sobre ellos, los enviaron" (Hechos 13:3, RVG). Y observe cómo lo describe Lucas en el mismo aliento siguiente: "Ellos entonces, enviados por el Espíritu Santo, descendieron a Seleucia" (Hechos 13:4, RVG). Antioquía los envió. El Espíritu Santo los envió. Ambas cosas son verdad. He aquí la primera iglesia que envía, y he aquí el patrón que nunca ha cambiado: el Espíritu llama obreros de en medio de una congregación que ora, ayuna y adora, y la iglesia les impone las manos y los envía hasta lo último de la tierra. Es la misma carga que vimos al Señor poner en nuestro corazón en la Gran Comisión.

blocks.en: Conclusion: We Are Acts 29
blocks.es_reference: Conclusión: Nosotros Somos Hechos 29

blocks.en: The book of Acts ends in the middle of the story, with Paul preaching in Rome, because the story was not over. Acts 1:8 is still the program of the church. The same Spirit who came at Pentecost still gives power. The same rings — Jerusalem, Judea and Samaria, the end of the earth — still widen outward, and they have widened far enough to reach us. The believer in Mexico, the lay person in the pew, the missionary on the field — every one of us stands in the long second volume, writing what we might call Acts chapter 29. The gospel is still spreading, and the only question is whether we will be among those who carry it.
blocks.es_reference: El libro de los Hechos termina en medio de la historia, con Pablo predicando en Roma, porque la historia no había terminado. Hechos 1:8 sigue siendo el programa de la iglesia. El mismo Espíritu que vino en Pentecostés todavía da poder. Los mismos anillos — Jerusalén, Judea y Samaria, lo último de la tierra — todavía se ensanchan hacia afuera, y se han ensanchado lo bastante para alcanzarnos. El creyente en México, el laico en la banca, el misionero en el campo — cada uno de nosotros está en el largo segundo volumen, escribiendo lo que podríamos llamar el capítulo 29 de los Hechos. El evangelio todavía se está esparciendo, y la única pregunta es si estaremos entre los que lo llevan.

fill.prompt: Luke says his Gospel told of all that Jesus ____ both to do and teach (Acts 1:1); Acts is volume two.
If the four Gospels are the vertical dimension of our faith, then Acts is the ____ dimension.
In Acts 1:8, the table of contents of the book, Jesus said, "you shall be ____ to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth."
At ____ the Spirit came, the church was born, and the hundred and twenty went out and turned the city upside down.
When ____ was martyred, a great persecution broke out and the believers were driven out of Jerusalem.
The verb Luke uses for "scattered" in Acts 8:4 comes from the root that means to ____, to fling seed across a plowed field.
Persecution did not dissipate the gospel; it ____ it.
God sent Peter to the house of ____, a Roman centurion, where the Holy Spirit fell on Gentiles.

sa.prompt: Explain why Acts is called 'volume two' and why the book has no ending.
sa.model: Acts is called 'volume two' because Luke's Gospel told all that Jesus began to do and teach, and Acts records what the risen, ascended Lord continued to do and teach through His Spirit-filled church. The book has no formal ending because that work is not finished — believers today are still living in the long second volume of what Christ continues to do.

sa.prompt: Show how Acts 1:8 serves as the table of contents of the whole book.
sa.model: Acts 1:8 serves as the table of contents because its three geographic terms map directly onto the book's structure: chapters 1-7 cover the witness in Jerusalem, chapters 8-12 carry it into Judea and Samaria, and chapters 13-28 take it to the end of the earth. The verse itself lays out the widening rings the whole book then narrates in order.

sa.prompt: Why does the lesson insist that power must come before the program? Use Acts 1:4–8.
sa.model: The lesson insists power must come before program because Jesus told the disciples not to depart from Jerusalem but to wait for the Promise of the Father, and only then would they receive power to be witnesses (Acts 1:4-8). Missions is the work of the Holy Spirit through the church; strategies and plans accomplish nothing without His power going before them.

sa.prompt: Describe the problem of the church that 'would not leave home,' and what it says about us.
sa.model: The church 'would not leave home' because even after Pentecost, with thousands saved, every new believer remained in Jerusalem — they had the command, the power, and the message, and still stayed in their comfortable surroundings rather than moving out to Judea, Samaria, and beyond. This exposes a danger in us too: it is easy to love the Great Commission in the abstract while never crossing the limits of our own comfortable Jerusalem.

sa.prompt: Explain the phrase 'scattered means sown,' including the Greek picture behind it.
sa.model: 'Scattered means sown' refers to Acts 8:4, where Luke's Greek verb for 'scattered' comes from the root meaning to sow — to fling seed across a plowed field, the same word Jesus used in the parable of the sower. Saul's persecution, which drove believers out of Jerusalem, did not destroy the gospel but disseminated it, as the scattered believers preached the word everywhere they went, unintentionally sowing a crop across Judea and Samaria.

sa.prompt: How did the barrier between Jew and Gentile fall? Use Peter and Cornelius.
sa.model: The barrier between Jew and Gentile fell when God gave Peter a vision on a rooftop in Joppa and then sent him to the house of Cornelius, a Roman centurion. There Peter declared that God shows no partiality but accepts anyone from any nation who fears Him and works righteousness (Acts 10:34-35), and when the Holy Spirit fell on the Gentiles just as at Pentecost, the matter was settled — the gospel was for all nations.

sa.prompt: Why is Antioch called the first sending church? Describe what happened in Acts 13.
sa.model: Antioch is called the first sending church because of what happened in Acts 13: while five leaders were fasting and ministering to the Lord, the Spirit said, 'Separate to Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.' The church then fasted, prayed, laid hands on them, and sent them away — the first recorded commissioning of missionaries by a local congregation.

sa.prompt: The lesson says 'Antioch sent them; the Holy Spirit sent them; both are true.' Explain what this means for missionary sending.
sa.model: The statement 'Antioch sent them; the Holy Spirit sent them; both are true' means that missionary sending is simultaneously a human and a divine act. Luke describes the church laying hands on them and sending them away, and in the very next breath says they were sent out by the Holy Spirit — the church's obedience does not compete with the Spirit's sovereign call, but is the very means through which He carries it out.

sa.prompt: Trace the three rings of Acts 1:8 through the book — Jerusalem, Judea and Samaria, the end of the earth — giving one event from each.
sa.model: The three rings of Acts 1:8 can be traced through the book: Jerusalem is filled by the events of Pentecost, where the Spirit came and three thousand were saved (Acts 2); Judea and Samaria are filled by the scattering after Stephen's martyrdom, when Philip preached in a Samaritan city (Acts 8); and the end of the earth is filled by the sending of Barnabas and Saul from Antioch, carrying the gospel to the Gentile world (Acts 13).

sa.prompt: What does it mean that the believer today is 'writing Acts chapter 29'? Apply it to the Mexican church and to yourself.
sa.model: To say the believer today is 'writing Acts chapter 29' means the story of the spreading gospel did not end when Luke stopped writing — the same Spirit, the same widening rings, and the same commission are still active, and every believer today, including the Mexican church, continues that unfinished story. For the individual student, it means recognizing that their own choices to go, send, or pray are the next lines of that same ongoing account.
